items.hook: The Airco DH.4 is a British two-seat biplane day bomber of the First World War.
items.body: It was designed by Geoffrey de Havilland for Airco, and was the first British two-seat light day-bomber capable of defending itself. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Charmed Life is a children's fantasy novel by British author Diana Wynne Jones published by Macmillan Children's Books in 1977.
items.body: It was the first Chrestomanci book and it remains a recommended introduction to the series. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Edinburgh international film festival showcases a Scottish industry in rude health
items.body:
This year’s festival is superpowered by a strong year for Scottish cinema, showing it can thrive under the ‘four dimensional perpetual catch-22’ of global ambitions

items.hook: The Charlie Madigan series is a collection of urban fantasy novels by author Kelly Gay.
items.body: The books present a future in which humanity has discovered two vastly different dimensions, making Atlanta a crossroads for various supernatural beings. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.body: Cole David Aldrich is an American former professional basketball player. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: ‘Remarkable’ discovery upends our understanding of how brains store memories
items.body: Memories in mice persisted even after they lost the connections that we thought were needed for recall, expanding our knowledge of memory in the mammalian brain

items.hook: Tammy and the Bachelor is a 1957 American romantic comedy film directed by Joseph Pevney and starring Debbie Reynolds as Tambrey "Tammy" Tyree, with Leslie Nielsen, Walter Brennan, Mala Powers, Sidney Blackmer, Mildred Natwick, Fay Wray, and Louise Beavers in supporting roles.
items.body: It is the first of the four Tammy films. One of those things you can't un-know.
